1.21.1.0.1001.0:
**New Feature ×2 · Editor ×1 · Community ×1 · Train ×1 · World ×1**

### 0.1001.0

**Dimensional carriages drift**

Dimensional carriages now drift the way carriages do. Build in one and your work is carried on down the line, with your name and changes travelling on.

- One in fifteen sealed (Bedrock Lock) dimensional carriages drifts: it uploads when edited and can arrive as another traveller's copy
- Builders are credited on entry, just like a drifting carriage
- New per-room Drift setting in the editor panel and /dt editor portals <room> drift

### 0.1000.0

**A quicker reassembly**

The stretch where the world stitches itself back together is now a little shorter, so you're back on solid ground sooner.

- The reassembling stretch is about a sixth shorter; everything after it arrives sooner

1.21.1.0.998.0:
**New Feature ×4 · World ×2 · Advancements ×2 · Bug Fix ×1 · Editor ×1 · Compatibility ×1**

### 0.998.0

**The journey takes a new route**

The line now runs through its landscapes in a different order, so some of the places you used to reach late in a run come sooner, and others come later.

- The stretches of the journey have been reshuffled.
- One stretch now blends gradually into the next instead of stopping at a hard edge.
- Structures along the line now sit into the land: the ground climbs over and into them, water flows through them where they stand in it, and they appear in every kind of terrain.
- They gather gradually rather than all at once, and a few now turn up earlier in the journey.

### 0.997.0

**Advancements reveal one step at a time**

The advancements screen now shows only what you've earned plus the next step ahead — everything further along stays hidden until you reach it.

### 0.996.0

**Faulthurst's Favourite hint in every language**

Faulthurst's Favourite now gives a hint before you earn it in every language, not just English.

**Effortless Building follows the editor's mirror, and whole rooms can be test-driven**

In the train editor, Effortless Building now respects a template's mirror settings. Lines, walls, cubes and breaks you make with it appear on the mirrored side too, and its ghost preview shows both halves before you place. One Ctrl+Z undoes both halves. Test the Carriage now works on whole rooms and whole groups, so you can walk through them before they ride the train.

- Effortless Building places and breaks are mirrored in mirror-enabled templates, including its own undo and redo
- The Effortless Building preview shows the mirrored half, even when you build into a template from outside it
- Test the Carriage works for whole rooms and whole groups, with Reseed and Back
- Whole groups can now be set as rare as one in every 1000 groups

**New ground behind you**

Head back along the train past where you boarded and the journey now carries on behind you, in its own order. But the train has to take you there: only ground you cover walking back along the train brings the next stretch closer, while jumping off or flying ahead just pushes it further away.

- Heading back past where you boarded now leads into new stretches
- Only distance covered on the train counts; getting off or flying ahead doesn't bring you closer
- Smoother edges where the strangest stretch gives way to ordinary land
1.21.1.0.995.0:
**New Feature ×1 · Compatibility ×1 · World ×1 · Behind the Scenes ×1**

### 0.995.0

**Some things hold together until you touch them**

Loose sand and gravel out in the stranger stretches of the journey no longer crumble away the moment you arrive. They hang where they were built, just like sand over a cave, until you disturb them.

- Loose blocks stay put until you mine or build next to them.

**CurseForge installs three companion mods alongside Dungeon Train**

On CurseForge, the OBS/Streamlabs check behind the Videos tab, the zapret/GoodbyeDPI check behind the connection warning, and one more small companion mod now install as their own mods next to Dungeon Train instead of living inside it. Nothing changes in-game, and Modrinth and manual installs keep them built in.

- The CurseForge app installs them for you automatically
- Modrinth and manual installs are unchanged
1.21.1.0.994.0:
**New Feature ×7 · Bug Fix ×3 · Compatibility ×3 · World ×2 · Menus & UI ×2 · Translations ×1 · Train ×1 · Mobs ×1 · Loot ×1 · Balance ×1**

### 0.994.0

**Dimensional carriages stay clean on later visits**

Deep into a run, a dimensional carriage could appear with bedrock where its void should be, and walking in could bounce you straight back onto the train with "This room lost its train". Each carriage now gets its own space again.

- Void rooms stay void — no stray bedrock from rooms you passed long ago
- No more being put back on the train the moment you step into a room

### 0.993.0

**Free Play explained the same way everywhere**

Every screen that mentions Free Play now explains it with the same words: advancements and stats won't be saved. Where you still have a choice to make, it adds that Free Play is a safe space to use hacks and cheats.

- The Free Play explanation now reads the same in chat, tooltips, menus and prompts
- Updated Free Play translations in every supported language

### 0.992.0

**No more holes in the scenery**

Along some of the stranger stretches of the line, the scenery beside the track now fills in first, instead of leaving square holes of empty sky for a while — or for good, if you moved on too quickly.

- Scenery closest to you fills in first
- No more square gaps left behind when the server is busy

### 0.991.0

**Bookshelves and honey blocks trade for 1 emerald**

Villagers now give 1 emerald for a bookshelf or a honey block. Bookshelves used to fetch far more.

### 0.990.0

**No more floating beds and villagers**

Villages caught in one of the stranger stretches of the journey no longer leave beds and villagers hanging in mid-air beside the track.

### 0.988.0

**Farmer's Delight**

Farmer's Delight isn't officially supported, but now it won't break the game at least.

### 0.987.0

**Faster creative sprint-flying**

Sprint-flying in creative is now 3× faster by default. Normal flight and flying up or down are unchanged. Use /dt flyspeed 1 to go back to vanilla speed, or pick any multiplier you like.

### 0.985.0

**Some whitelisted mods need a recent Dungeon Train**

A few mods on the whitelist are only approved on newer versions of Dungeon Train, because they rely on support those versions added. Run one on an older version and the run is Free Play until you update.

- Update Dungeon Train to keep a mod like Catalogue on the whitelist

### 0.984.0

**The whitelist now covers settings changed mid-run**

Changing a Dungeon Train balance setting while you're playing, whether in the settings screen or an in-game config editor, now puts that run into Free Play for good, just like using a tuning command. Changing it back before you quit no longer hides it.

- How the train's mobs fight and scavenge now counts as a balance setting
- So does whether your backpack survives death, and how big it can grow
- The one-click settings reset puts these back to default along with everything else

**Chat tells you when a new version drops**

If a new Dungeon Train version is released while you're playing, a line appears in chat saying which version is out and how long ago it dropped, with a link to what's new.

- Only real releases are announced — never the small automatic ones
- Turn it off in Options > Dungeon Train > New Version Chat
1.21.1.0.983.0:
**Bug Fix ×1 · Compatibility ×1**

### 0.983.0

**New worlds load again with ModernFix installed**

Starting a new world with ModernFix installed — it ships in the modpack — could crash with "Exception generating new chunk", or leave the loading screen sitting at 33% for good. Both are fixed.

- No change to how the world generates: the same seed still gives the same world, with ModernFix or without.
1.21.1.0.982.0:
# Dimensions Overhaul 0.982.0

## Number of dimensions
A HUGE boost to the number of dimensions the train travels through. Many custom made for DT, some you may already know and love.

## Shorter Dimensions
Dimensions are now short, pass through more quicker, but it will take longer to pass through them all.

# The Whitelist for Mods
Moving from blacklist to whitelist. Unless whitelisted, mods put you into freeplay. 
The game will boot regardless, only whitelisted will enable high-scores.

## Modpack Additions
* **Advanced Shulkerboxes:** 
* **Sable Pathfinder:** *(Modrinth only for now)*
* **Pigman Villagers:** ;)

## Train Editor Tools
The train editor has undergone some big changes, make it work much better
* **Test the Carriage** works on every carriage and contents template. Ctrl/Cmd+R re-rolls it
* **Frames:** build your own to dress terrain dimensional carriages
* **Doors, beds and tall plants** in block variants, with a new Span button
* **Menus stay put** instead of following you, update as soon as you save, and no longer freeze on first open
* **New** works for whole rooms and groups
* **Save as new** on built-in templates, or keep a local edit
* **Info panel** shows a build's lights and loot
* **My Builds:** delete builds, and tell the reviewer about your build when you submit
* Cmd/Ctrl-click deletes saved prefabs in the creative menu
* Effortless Building breaks now clear block variants
* Big shared builds keep their chest loot, and loading survives a busy server
* Templates with thousands of block variants no longer lag

## Bug Fixes
* No more freezes when editing the train or saving
* Distant Horizons no longer crashes on Mac
* Dedicated servers now create Dungeon Train worlds
* Eyes of ender lead to the same stronghold every time
* Crops in dimensional carriages stay planted
* Trees no longer turn the track into a tunnel

## Bug fixes
- New Biomes are cosmetics focused. New items and mobs on the train will be coming later.
1.21.1.0.934.0:
**New Feature ×2 · World ×2 · New Content ×1 · Train ×1 · Balance ×1**

### 0.934.0

**The far reaches get stranger still**

Past the last place that made sense, the world keeps changing the longer you ride — borrowing from places you would never expect to see from a train, with more waiting to be found the deeper you go.

- One of the stranger stretches of the journey now runs longer.
- What drifts past the window changes as you go, and the sky changes with it.
- Keep riding: there is more to find out there than there used to be.

### 0.933.0

**New bookshelf carriage interior and refreshed seating**

A new book-lined carriage interior can now turn up on the train, and the seating interiors have been rearranged with fresh layouts. Book-themed interiors also show up a little less often, so carriages feel more varied.

- New book-lined carriage interior
- Refreshed seating carriage layouts
- Book-themed interiors appear slightly less often

### 0.932.0

**The sky has its own ideas out there**

Somewhere far down the line, past the last place that made sense, the sky itself stops being what you remember. Keep riding — you'll know it when you see it.

- One of the stranger stretches of the journey now runs longer.
- The deeper you go, the less the sky, light and music feel like home.
1.21.1.0.931.0:
**New Feature ×9 · Editor ×7 · Train ×5 · World ×3 · Loot ×3 · Menus & UI ×3 · New Content ×2 · Advancements ×2 · Bug Fix ×1 · Community ×1 · Behind the Scenes ×1**

### 0.931.0

**Block variants can spawn switched on**

In the Train Editor's block-variant menu, variants of blocks that hold a toggled state — trapdoors, doors, fence gates, levers and copper bulbs — now have an On / R / Off pill beside the half pill. Set a trapdoor to spawn open, a lever thrown or a copper bulb lit, or pick R to roll it per carriage. Blocks that fall back when a signal stops (lamps, pistons, buttons) don't get the pill. Existing builds keep spawning exactly as before.

- On / R / Off pill on trapdoors, doors, fence gates, levers and copper bulbs
- Random rolls per carriage, so a corridor can mix open and closed trapdoors
- Editor preview shows the chosen state; Random blinks between both

**Deeper floors in dimensional carriages**

An endless plain's floor can now be laid several blocks deep instead of one. Set it from the Floor row and a water floor becomes a pool you can dive into, a stone one solid ground you can dig.

- Step the depth up and down right on the Floor row.
- Water, lava and stone floors all take a depth.

**The line goes on — and up**

Further down the track than anyone has ridden, after a long stretch of ordinary country, the world stops making sense in a whole new way. Keep riding — you'll know it when you get there.

- Another new stretch of the journey, past the last one
- A new advancement for those who make it that far

**Point a block variant at a lock group in one click**

In the block-variant menu, hold a variant clipboard copied from a locked cell and shift-click a row to turn it into a reference to that group. Shift-click an existing reference with a different clipboard to point it somewhere else.

- Shift-click a row with a variant clipboard to make it a group reference.
- Retarget an existing reference the same way.

**Carriage rooms dress for the journey**

Shops, workshops, libraries, mazes and many other carriage rooms now take on the stone and wood of the stretch the train is crossing, so the same room looks different from one stage to the next. The library also gains a new shelf-lined layout.

- Carriage interiors change their materials as the journey goes on.
- A new library layout, wall to wall with bookshelves.
- The leatherworker stocks enchanted armour.

**The strange stretches run longer**

Some of the stranger places the line runs through now last longer before the world settles back to normal.

- A few of the stranger stretches of the journey take longer to cross.
- Worlds started before this update may show a seam where the new layout meets land you have already seen.

### 0.930.0

**The train passes through somewhere new**

There is another dimension on the line now, waiting further down the track. Keep riding — you'll know it when you get there.

- A new stretch of the journey for the train to cross
- A new advancement for those who make it that far

**Swap a block variant without rebuilding the row**

In the block-variant menu, hold the block you want and shift-click a row's name to swap it in. The row keeps its weight, rotation lock and half setting, so retheming a cell is one click per row instead of remove-and-add.

- Shift-click a row name to replace it with the block in your hand.
- Orientation and settings carry over.

### 0.929.0

**Whole carriages keep the mobs, pictures and loot their builder placed**

A whole carriage — a room or a group built as one piece — arrived empty of everything that was not a block. The armour stands, paintings, minecarts and mobs its builder stood in it were saved with the build and then never appeared, in the editor or on the train, and opening the build again wrote them out of the file for good. Containers in a downloaded whole carriage came with no loot either. Everything the builder placed now comes with the build.

- Armour stands, paintings, minecarts and mobs stand where their builder left them, in the editor and on a moving train.
- Chests in a whole carriage downloaded from another builder carry the loot they were set up with.
- Saving a whole carriage keeps what is standing in it, instead of quietly emptying it.

**The prison and the treasure reading room got a pass**

Two of the fancy carriage interiors were reworked. The broken prison now only turns up in the stages its stonework suits, rather than in every one, and picked up some detailing and a potion stash. The treasure reading room traded half its wall of chests for bookshelves, and the chests that remain now roll their contents from a spread of supply, trade and library stashes instead of holding the same things every time.

- The broken prison appears in stone, spruce, oak, mangrove, jungle, darkwood and acacia stages.
- The treasure reading room's chests vary from one carriage to the next.

### 0.928.0

**No more rain in the Train Editor**

The Train Editor now sits under clear skies. Rain and thunderstorms used to roll across your plots and darken everything you were building, even though the editor is a void with nothing for rain to land on — now the weather stays off, the same way the clock stays at noon. An editor world you left in the middle of a storm comes back clear.

- Weather is off by default in every Train Editor world, new or existing.
- A storm you quit in is cleared when the world loads again.

**Water floors and lava skies in dimensional carriages**

The editor's Floor and Roof rows now take a bucket as readily as a block, so an endless plain can be open water underfoot or a sheet of lava overhead. The plain stays whole — no rock seams where one stretch meets the next.

- Hold a filled bucket and press the Floor or Roof row.
- Water and lava planes flow into each other cleanly across the whole plain.

**Translation records caught up with the bucket wording**

Bookkeeping only: the translation records now match the reworded editor message, so the language checks pass again.
1.21.1.0.927.0:
**Bug Fix ×2 · Editor ×2 · Train ×2 · New Feature ×1 · Community ×1 · Menus & UI ×1**

### 0.927.0

**Whole carriages: rooms and groups you build as one piece**

The Train Editor has a new Whole section, first in the row. A Room is a complete carriage saved as one piece, shell and interior together; a Group is a whole run of three. Rooms roll into the train alongside the ordinary shells, groups replace an entire carriage group one in every N, and both come from a pool you weight, gate and stage like any other template. Builds from other creators can be loaded straight into the room pool, and Firefly_on_ytb's cave and jungle temple ride the train as the first two whole rooms.

- New Whole section in the editor, the X menu and the Train Editor picker, with Room and Group tabs
- Whole rooms spawn like shared carriages; whole groups replace a carriage group one in every N, set beside the Group title or on the Settings page
- Block variants (Z) and container contents (C) work inside whole plots and roll at spawn
- Load another creator's carriage or contents build straight into the room pool
- Two bundled whole rooms by Firefly_on_ytb; Collapseofsmth's five rooms join a new featurefancy contents group

### 0.926.0

**The train is all there when you come back**

Wander off the line and return, and every carriage is waiting for you again straight away — no more watching the train reappear one piece at a time, or thinking half of it had vanished.

- Carriages come back all at once, not one by one.
- Sitting in the pause menu no longer gets logged as a server freeze.

**Go here on a portal plot faces the menu again**

Teleporting onto the portal carriage or a portal contents plot from the editor's X menu now lands you facing its menu, a few blocks in front of it — it used to be just behind your back on those longer plots.

- Portal carriage and portal contents plots: menu straight ahead after Go here.
1.21.1.0.925.0:
**New Feature ×1 · New Content ×1 · Bug Fix ×1 · Community ×1 · Train ×1 · Loot ×1 · Menus & UI ×1 · Balance ×1**

### 0.925.0

**New carriage builds and weight tweaks**

A couple of new carriage builds can now appear on the train, and some spawn weights were adjusted.

### 0.924.0

**Streaming? The menu nudges you to share your link**

If OBS or Streamlabs is open when you reach the main menu, the red Videos icon stretches out a "Streaming? Share link!" tag, and the Submit button on the Videos page pulses red. A small × above the tag hides it for the session. Nothing about it leaves your machine — it only looks at whether the app is running.

- Videos icon on the title screen grows a "Streaming? Share link!" tag while OBS/Streamlabs is running
- Submit-a-video button on the Videos page pulses red at the same time
- Click the × above the tag to hide it until next launch

**The End portal brings you home**

Beat the dragon and step through the portal — you land back on the train, right where you belong, with everything you carried.

- No more waking up in an empty world after the End.
- Works every time you come back through, not just the first.
1.21.1.0.923.0:
**Bug Fix ×1 · Train ×1**

### 0.923.0

**Dimensional carriages are built from the right blocks all the way through**

A dimensional carriage in the Nether stretch could come out in the wrong wood — warped on the way in, oak further along — and the extra ways out of an endless room could show the editor's stage blocks instead of real ones. Every part of a dimensional carriage now uses the blocks the carriage itself was built with.

- Dimensional carriages keep their stage's blocks throughout — warped stays warped, stone stays stone
- Extra exit corridors in endless rooms no longer show placeholder stage blocks
1.21.1.0.922.0:
**Bug Fix ×9 · Editor ×9 · Behind the Scenes ×5 · Performance ×3 · Translations ×2 · Multiplayer ×1 · Train ×1 · World ×1**

### 0.922.0

**Mining and fighting on the train no longer lag behind you**

In single-player the train's physics was doing more work each tick than the ride needed, and on a long train it dragged the whole game behind you: blocks you had mined broke late, hits landed late, and mobs moved as if underwater. The train now runs lighter, so what you do happens when you do it.

- Blocks break and drop the moment you finish mining them.
- Hits, knockback and mob movement keep up with you.

### 0.921.0

**Test the Carriage no longer freezes low-end PCs on the way in or out**

Entering or leaving Test the Carriage with Skybox Blocks switched off used to rebuild every chunk in view at once — on a low-end PC that was a long stall going in and a hard freeze coming back. Now only the chunks that actually hold a Skybox Block are redrawn, so the test starts and ends as quickly as the teleport itself. The room's fog and daylight also stopped flickering on and off during a test.

- Only Skybox Block chunks are redrawn when a test starts or ends, not the whole view
- Dimensional-carriage fog and sky no longer switch on and off every tick while you test

### 0.920.0

**Beds aboard the train stop exploding after the Nether**

A bed placed inside a carriage that had rolled through the Nether could still blow up long after the train was back in the overworld. Beds on board now behave like the world outside the window: safe in the overworld, still deadly while the train is inside the Nether or the End.

### 0.919.0

**Entering the plot you are already in keeps your edits — from the track roof too**

Stepping back into the plot you are standing in is a walk to its menu, not a reload. Every plot now agrees on that, and the track tile is no exception: Go here or Enter from its roof no longer wipes what you built.

- Go here / Enter from inside any plot keeps unsaved edits, track tile roof included.
- Dimensional carriage names typed in any case land in the right room.

### 0.918.0

**Beds no longer claim to set a respawn point**

Sleeping in a bed on the train used to answer with 'Respawn point set — aboard the train' and similar lines, which read as if the bed worked like a normal spawn. Every bed message now says plainly that no respawn point was set — the train is your only way back, wherever it has rolled. All 20 languages carry the corrected wording.

### 0.917.0

**Every editor lands you the same way**

Where you arrive when you enter a plot — on the roof facing its menu, in its front doorway, or at its centre — used to be worked out separately by each of the seven editors. It is now decided in one place, so carriages, dimensional carriages, parts, pillars, tracks and tunnels can never drift apart. Nothing moves for you: every landing is exactly where it was.

- One landing rule shared by all seven editors, covered by tests for each way in.
- A plot with no doorway simply lands you at its centre — no special cases per editor.

### 0.916.0

**Pictures stay on the wall for good**

The fix that stopped Fast Paintings pictures dropping off the wall whenever a build, plot or carriage was loaded now lives in one place instead of twelve, and a build-time check makes sure no future loader can bring the bug back.

- One named setting owns how every template is stamped into the world, with the reason written down once.
- A test fails the build if any loader ever reaches for the old setting that popped pictures.

### 0.915.0

**The rest of the editor commands confirm in chat again**

The same 0.908.0 regression that silenced the editor enter lines also hit a further fourteen editor messages — setting a carriage, track or contents weight, flipping contents, baking a stage palette, replacing a block across a stage, the part-plot enter line, the "target block is outside the plot" warnings, and the portal-carriage save confirmation. All of them now reach chat instead of failing into the log.

- Weight, flip, stage bake and stage replaceblock commands report their result and the file they wrote
- Every remaining message the mod prints is now checked by a build-time test so this class of bug cannot ship again

### 0.914.0

**Loading a build shows it, even from inside the plot**

Loading a build from the relay while standing in its plot now brings the new blocks in with you. Before, the plot kept showing what was there already, and saving would quietly write that back over the build you had just loaded.

- Load and Replace refresh the plot you are standing in.
- Go here and the panel's Enter still keep your unsaved edits.

### 0.912.0

**Outdated clients are turned away at login instead of being kicked mid-session**

Joining a server with a Dungeon Train build older than the server's could work at first and then drop you the moment you used a plot panel in the editor, because the two builds disagreed about what that message looked like. The network version now says so up front: a mismatched client sees the usual mod-mismatch screen at login, with both versions listed, and a matching one joins as before. A check in the build pipeline keeps this from slipping again.

- Client and server builds that disagree are refused at login, not dropped mid-game
- The mismatch screen names both versions so you know which side to update

**Editor plots enter cleanly again**

Entering any editor plot — a carriage, tunnel, pillar, contents or track plot — or creating a new one printed a red "enter failed" error in chat even though you had arrived. The green "entered … plot at x, y, z" line is back and the error is gone.

- Affects every editor enter and new/clone command since v0.907.

### 0.911.0

**Editor: relay Load result lands on the right build**

Loading a build from the X menu while clicking other tiles no longer credits the result to the wrong one.

**Entering a built-up plot no longer stalls the server**

Pressing Enter on a plot whose doorway and door row are blocked — a raised floor, a wall across the door, a pillar in the centre — used to freeze the game for a moment on large rooms while it looked for somewhere to put you. It now finds the nearest free spot straight away, and you land in exactly the same place as before.

- Enter on a 64×64×64 room with a raised floor is instant instead of dropping a few ticks
- Landing spot is unchanged — still the nearest free cell inside, never in the wall

### 0.910.0

**Backrooms carriage re-saved in current editor format**

The Backrooms dimensional carriage's variant data was re-saved from the editor in the current format. Nothing changes in-game.
1.21.1.0.909.0:
**Bug Fix ×1 · Compatibility ×1**

### 0.909.0

**Keep Trim is built in again for Modrinth and manual installs**

Installing Dungeon Train from Modrinth or by hand no longer fails with "requires keeptrim — not installed". Keep Trim's Modrinth page is still awaiting review, so it now ships inside the Dungeon Train jar; CurseForge keeps installing it as its own mod.

- Modrinth and manual installs load without a separate Keep Trim download
- CurseForge app users are unaffected — the separately installed copy still takes precedence
1.21.1.0.908.0:
**Editor ×8 · Bug Fix ×5 · Menus & UI ×5 · New Feature ×4 · Compatibility ×3 · Behind the Scenes ×2 · New Content ×1 · Community ×1 · Translations ×1 · Train ×1**

### 0.908.0

**Loading a relay build into the editor tells you what happened**

In the editor's Templates menu, loading somebody's relay build used to look like nothing happened — big builds take a while and the result line was hidden. The button now shows Loading… until the build is in, the result is shown above it, and a build you already have says so instead of offering itself again.

- Load, Load as sub-variant and Load as a copy grey out and read Loading… while the build comes down
- The outcome (loaded, name already in use, couldn't load) is shown where you can see it
- A build already loaded as a sub-variant is recognised as loaded across restarts
- Hold Shift on a loaded build to load it again as a copy under a free name

**Pictures stay on the wall when a build is stamped into the editor**

Fast Paintings pictures wider than two blocks fell off the wall as items whenever a template was stamped into an editor or builder plot — loading a relay build, entering a plot, Reset. They now stay hung.

**New dimensional carriage: Grandisola Generator by CorporalJackShep**

A 64-block generator hall with 31 pictures, added to the house set of dimensional carriages (levels 376–415).

### 0.907.0

**Editor teleports land where you want to be**

Go here and the template list now put you on the plot roof right in front of its floating menu, facing it — no more landing in the middle of a long build with the menu behind you. Go here is offered even while you're standing in that template, and hopping back to your own plot no longer reloads it, so unsaved work stays put. The panel's Enter button drops you in the front doorway facing in (hold shift for the centre), and every inside landing finds a free spot instead of putting you in a wall.

- Go here lands you in front of the plot's menu, looking at it
- Go here works from inside the template too, without reloading your unsaved edits
- Enter puts you in the front doorway of carriages, contents and dimensional carriages; shift-click for the centre
- Inside landings step to the nearest free space rather than into a block

### 0.906.0

**The build editor speaks your language**

Every menu, panel and chat line in the build editor now shows in the language you play in — the X menu, the block-variant and container panels, the plot labels, the Train Builder picker and everything the editor commands say back. All 20 languages have a first machine translation, and the Translate tool has a new "Build editor" filter so translators can polish that body on its own, or skip it.

- Editor menus, plot labels and command feedback translated in all 20 languages
- Translate tool: new "Build editor" body — the game's own text is no longer mixed with editor jargon
- Train Builder picker tiles that were still English in 18 languages are now translated

### 0.905.0

**PlayerMob 0.99.0**

Dungeon Train now builds against PlayerMob 0.99.0, whose Creative editor can introduce a mob to nearby PlayerMobs and players and mirror a pair's feelings. Update PlayerMob to 0.99.0 to use it; 0.98.0 remains supported.

### 0.904.0

**Every Dungeon Train build ships as a beta, even re-uploads**

Dungeon Train is still pre-1.0, so every build is published as a beta on CurseForge, Modrinth and GitHub. One CurseForge re-upload (0.692.0) slipped out marked as a full release, which made the CurseForge app prefer that old file over newer builds for anyone on the default Release filter. The release channel is now decided in one place for every upload path, so that can't happen again.

- Recovery re-uploads to CurseForge use the same beta/release channel as the original release.
- Modpack uploads on CurseForge and Modrinth follow the same rule.

### 0.903.0

**Editor: place mobs like blocks**

A new Settings row, Mobs | Blocks | Live (default Blocks), changes what a spawn egg does in an editor plot. Under Blocks the mob stands frozen on the cell you clicked, facing you, and one hit removes it — so you can place and clear mobs the way you place blocks, and they stay where you put them until you save. Variant cells that can roll a mob now show that mob standing on the cell, taking its turn in the same preview cycle the block variants use. Live keeps vanilla eggs. On a real train the mobs come to life as normal.

- Settings → Mobs | Blocks | Live: eggs place a still, one-hit mob in editor plots (Blocks) or a normal wandering one (Live)
- Variant cells with a mob entry show the mob on the cell, cycling with the other entries instead of a command block
- Mobs authored frozen wake up when their carriage is stamped onto the train

**Group references can be added to any block**

In the block-variant menu you can now add a group reference straight onto a plain block. The block you point at becomes the first choice and the group the second, so you no longer have to add a second block first just to unlock the option.

- Add a locked group's clipboard to any block in one step — no placeholder second block needed.
- Adding a block that a group reference happens to display as no longer reports it as already in the cell.

**Block-variant cells show a ghost cube instead of a command block**

In the Train Editor, a variant cell that can roll to nothing — or to a mob — now stands as a translucent ghost cube rather than a command block. It reads as empty at a glance, and you can place blocks against it with a plain right-click; no more holding shift to get past the command block's screen.

- Empty and mob slots in a variant cell show a see-through placeholder block, not a command block
- Right-click places against a placeholder without shift
- Existing builds pick the new look up automatically the next time you open them

**Save-as keeps a template's block variants**

Saving a bundled carriage, interior or part under a new name in the editor no longer drops its block variants — the new copy keeps every variant cell the original had.

- Contents, carriage and part editors all carry variants across a save-as

### 0.895.0

**See when this life has ruled an advancement out — and track the ones you care about**

Some advancements can only be earned within a single life, and one wrong move ends the attempt. The advancements screen now shows it: a tile this life has ruled out fades and its hint gains a red "Lost for this life." line, clearing again when your next life begins. Click a single-life advancement to track it — it gets a yellow halo, and the moment this life rules it out a red-bordered pop-up tells you. Streak-style advancements can be tracked too; those pop up an amber "Streak reset" instead, since their count simply starts over.

- Advancements ruled out for the current life fade in the tree and say "Lost for this life." on hover
- Click a single-life advancement to track it; a red pop-up warns you the moment it's lost, an amber one when a streak resets
- Works on both the vanilla advancements screen and Better Advancements

### 0.894.0

**A secret goal no longer needs company**

One of the train's hidden goals quietly asked for something only another player's arrival could hand you — so playing alone, it could never be finished. It can now.

- Everything it asks for can be found on your own.

### 0.893.0

**Your Ender Chest survives a crash**

If the game crashed, your Ender Chest used to come back as it was at the end of the previous session — everything you had put in during the crashed one was gone. It now keeps whatever was in it at the last autosave, so a crash costs you at most a few minutes, the same as the rest of your inventory. Ender Chest Persistence 0.5.0 is now required; the CurseForge and Modrinth apps update it for you.

- Ender Chest contents are saved every autosave and whenever you switch game mode, not only when you leave the world
- Requires Ender Chest Persistence 0.5.0 (auto-installed by the CurseForge / Modrinth apps)

**Paste variant clipboards across a whole floor, wall or box with Effortless Building**

In the editor, a variant clipboard now works with Effortless Building's shape modes. Pick Floor, Wall or Cube with the clipboard in hand and every cell of the shape gets the copied variant pool in one go — lock group, copy settings and any container loot included — instead of one cell per click. One Ctrl+Z undoes the whole paste.

- Floor / Wall / Cube (and the mirror, array and radial modifiers) all work with a variant clipboard
- A plain right-click still pastes a single cell

### 0.892.0

**Paintings now hang properly on the train and in your builds**

Paintings used to be the one decoration you could not trust on a moving carriage or in a saved build — they would drift, vanish, or fall off when a carriage was flipped. Dungeon Train now requires Fast Paintings (and its Moonlight library), which turns paintings into solid blocks: they ride the train like any other block, save into templates and shared carriages exactly as you hung them, and when a carriage interior comes out mirrored the painting simply re-hangs on the wall it now stands beside. The CurseForge and Modrinth apps install both mods for you; if you install by hand, grab Fast Paintings and Moonlight for NeoForge 1.21.1.

- Paintings hang solidly on moving carriages and in the builder — no more drifting or falling off
- Saved builds and shared carriages keep every painting, size and picture included
- Mirrored carriage interiors keep their paintings; they re-hang on the opposite wall instead of dropping
- Two new required mods, Fast Paintings and Moonlight — auto-installed by the CurseForge and Modrinth apps

### 0.891.0

**On CurseForge, Dungeon Backup and the Sable fence & trapdoor fix are now their own mods**

If you play through the CurseForge app or the CurseForge modpack, two pieces that were built into Dungeon Train now arrive as separate required mods that the app installs and updates for you: Dungeon Backup (rolling restore points of your Dungeon Train data, with a recovery prompt if it ever goes missing) and Sable Fence & Trapdoor Fix (no more jittering when you stand on a fence post tucked under a trapdoor or carpet on a moving carriage). Their own CurseForge pages now get the credit. On Modrinth, and for anyone who installs the jar by hand, nothing changes — both are still built into Dungeon Train. Nothing changes in play either way.

- CurseForge app and CurseForge modpack install Dungeon Backup and Sable Fence & Trapdoor Fix as separate mods
- Modrinth and manual installs keep them built in — no extra downloads
- No change to backups, /dtbackup, /dtrestore or the fence fix in play

Particle Effects ships enabled in both the CurseForge and Modrinth modpacks; it is client-only, so servers and existing installs need nothing.

- Unique textured particle per vanilla status effect, on you and on mobs
- Client-only — nothing changes server-side or in saves

**Advancements can be switched off, or out of the final tally, without an update**

### 0.885.0

**Player heads remember the dead in every carriage**

The player heads decorating the train wear the skin and name of a real player whose run ended in that carriage. Until now that only worked in every third carriage — deaths are recorded per carriage group, and the other two carriages in each group asked for a record nobody could ever match, so they always fell back to a stock face. Every carriage now draws from its group's fallen players.

- Heads in carriages 1, 2, 4, 5… now show real fallen players, not just carriages 0, 3, 6…
- Three times fewer relay requests: one per carriage group instead of one per carriage

### 0.884.0

**Your Ender Chest is now protected against being wiped**

Ender Chest Persistence is updated to 0.4.0. Your chest now lives outside the modpack instance, so reinstalling the pack or moving launchers keeps it, and the mod keeps an automatic backup of the last non-empty contents — if the file is ever damaged it is restored from that backup instead of being emptied. Existing chests are carried across automatically on your next login.

- Ender Chest survives pack reinstalls and launcher moves (stored in your system's app-data folder)
- Automatic <uuid>.dat.bak of the last non-empty chest; a damaged file self-heals from it and is never overwritten with an empty one
- Requires Ender Chest Persistence 0.4.0 — CurseForge/Modrinth apps install it with the pack

### 0.883.0

**Free Play Ender Chest can expand to 114 slots**

In Free Play, your Ender Chest now has an Expand button. Press it and the chest grows from 27 to 114 slots: three more rows above the ones you know, plus a five-column wing on each side, like Edible Backpacks' panels. Your existing items stay exactly where they were. The expanded chest travels with you to every Free Play world, and a Shrink button takes it back to normal whenever the extra slots are empty. Ordinary runs are untouched — the bigger chest only exists for the separate Free Play chest, so nothing from it can ever reach a legit stash.

- Expand button in the Free Play Ender Chest: 27 → 114 slots (3 rows above, 5 columns each side)
- Shrink back any time the extra slots are empty
- Persists across every Free Play world; legit runs keep the vanilla chest

### 0.882.0

**Editor: observers stay quiet while you build**

Observers in an editor plot no longer fire on their own while the editor shows you things — the variant preview cycle, a row click in the variant menu, a plot reset. And there is a new Observers On / Off switch in the editor Settings: switch it Off and every observer inside a plot stays quiet even for blocks you place and break by hand, so you can wire a contraption without setting it off. Trains in play worlds are untouched.

- Variant previews, menu previews, mirror stamps and plot resets never pulse an observer
- Settings → Observers | On | Off — Off mutes observers in editor plots, hand edits included; remembered per world
- Wallminer trap: TNT joins the wall-cell variant pool; new 'very_dangerouds_1' trap contents

### 0.881.0

**Train Editor pause menu keeps Save and Quit**

The Train Editor world's pause menu no longer offers Abandon This Run — there is no run to abandon there, and taking it killed the author. It now shows the normal Save and Quit to Title, with My Builds above it, and Shift still reveals Exit to Title | Quit Game.

- Train Editor: Esc menu shows Save and Quit to Title instead of the red Abandon This Run
- My Builds stays above the exit; Shift still swaps in Exit to Title | Quit Game

### 0.880.0

**Stages tab previews show each stage's real blocks, and ✓ selects the stage**

In the Train Editor's Stages tab, every wood stage's preview used to look identical — the tiles were drawn with the raw stage placeholder blocks instead of that stage's wood. Previews now resolve through each stage's palette, so acacia, birch, cherry, warped and the rest each show their own blocks. The ✓ button on the preview pane now selects the shown stage: the stage block icons, the placed placeholder textures and the carriage plot previews all follow it, and clicking again deselects. Linking a template to a stage lives on the template's own sheet.

- Stage previews stamp with the stage's real palette instead of placeholder blocks
- ✓ on the stage preview selects (or deselects) that stage — icons, textures and plots follow

### 0.879.0

**Editor sheet keeps its block count when a build holds an armour stand**

In the editor screen, the Blocks line of a build's data sheet went blank as soon as the build contained an entity such as an armour stand. The count now always shows, with the entity and container tallies beside it when there is room.

- Blocks line reads e.g. '312 · 1 entities' instead of disappearing
- On a narrow window only the tallies drop off, never the count
